summary: Defines a Proxy Mobile IPv6 extension, an option called LMA-Controlled-MAG-Session-Params. It lets the local mobility anchor tell a mobile access gateway which values to use for settings such as heartbeat and binding refresh parameters.

eli5.summary: A boss at head office tells each branch manager exactly how often to check in. This adds a message that lets the boss set those check-in times.

questions: what is the lma controlled mag parameters option
how does the lma set mag heartbeat timers
what is option type 62 in proxy mobile ipv6
what happens if an lcmp parameter is zero
subtitle: How a Proxy Mobile IPv6 anchor can tell its gateways which re-registration and heartbeat timers to use.

tldr.problem: A large Proxy Mobile IPv6 network can have tens of thousands of gateways, and keeping their timer settings consistent is hard. Aggressive values for re-registration and heartbeats can create heavy signaling load on the anchor.
tldr.mechanism: The local mobility anchor (LMA) adds a new option, LMA-Controlled MAG Parameters, to its Proxy Binding Acknowledge message. The option carries sub-options that make the mobile access gateway (MAG) overwrite its local re-registration and heartbeat timers.
tldr.outcome: Operators can set these timers centrally on the LMA and get a predictable signaling load. This is a Proposed Standard and it has not been obsoleted or updated.

today: RFC 8127 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2017. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why the Anchor Should Set the Timers
sections.content:
In Proxy Mobile IPv6 (PMIPv6, RFC 5213), mobile access gateways (MAGs) register devices with a local mobility anchor (LMA). A large residential deployment can have tens of thousands of MAGs spread across many locations. Managing them one by one is operationally hard, and it is just as hard to keep their configuration consistent.

Timer values matter because aggressive settings for re-registration and heartbeat intervals can put considerable signaling load on the LMA. This document adds an option that lets the LMA control those parameters on the MAG. The RFC points to the re-registration frequency from RFC 5213 and the heartbeat frequency from RFC 5847. Service providers get central control and a deterministic signaling load on the LMA.
sections.eli5: If every branch manager picked their own check-in time, the head office phone would ring all day. Letting head office pick the times keeps things calm and predictable.

sections.title: The LCMP Option and Its Sub-Options
sections.content:
The LMA-Controlled MAG Parameters (LCMP) option is a mobility header option. It can be included only in the Proxy Binding Acknowledge (PBA) message, and a PBA MUST NOT contain more than one instance. Its Type is 62. Length is an 8-bit count of the option's octets, excluding the Type and Length fields. The option has an alignment requirement of 4n+2.

The option MUST contain at least one LCMP sub-option, in any order. Each sub-option has an 8-bit LCMP Type, an 8-bit LCMP Length and the sub-option data, and sub-options have an alignment requirement of 4n. The types defined are 0 (Reserved), 1 (Binding Re-registration Control) and 2 (Heartbeat Control).

The Binding Re-registration Control sub-option has an LCMP Length of 6 and may appear at most once in the LCMP option. It carries three 16-bit fields:

  • Re-registration-Start-Time: how many time units before the PMIPv6 binding lifetime expires the refresh process should start. One time unit is 4 seconds.
  • Initial-Retransmission-Time: the minimum delay in seconds before the first Proxy Binding Update (PBU) retransmission of the exponential backoff.
  • Maximum-Retransmission-Time: the maximum delay in seconds before the last PBU retransmission of the exponential backoff.

The Heartbeat Control sub-option also has an LCMP Length of 6 and carries three 16-bit fields:

  • HB-Interval: seconds to wait after a successful heartbeat exchange (request followed by response) before the next one can be triggered.
  • HB-Retransmission-Delay: the minimum delay in seconds before a heartbeat message is retransmitted.
  • HB-Max-Retransmissions: the maximum number of heartbeat retransmissions.
sections.eli5: The option is a small envelope with notes inside. One note says when to renew your registration and how to retry. The other says how often to say hello and how many times to try again.

sections.title: Configuration Variables on the LMA
sections.content:
The LMA is configured through system management, and the configured values MUST survive server reboots and service restarts. Two flags switch the features on: EnableLCMPSubOptReregControl and EnableLCMPSubOptHeartbeatControl. Both default to 0, which means the feature is disabled.

The value variables MAY be defined per binding, per cluster of bindings, per peering MAG, per cluster of peering MAGs or any other custom grouping. Whatever the granularity, the LMA MUST be able to determine the value for every individual binding. The defaults are:

  • LCMPReregistrationStartTime: 10 units of 4 seconds each.
  • LCMPInitialRetransmissionTime: 1 second, the same as INITIAL_BINDACK_TIMEOUT in RFC 5213.
  • LCMPMaximumRetransmissionTime: 32 seconds, the same as MAX_BINDACK_TIMEOUT in RFC 5213.
  • LCMPHeartbeatInterval: 60 seconds. It SHOULD NOT be less than 30 or more than 3600 seconds, and MAY be derived from HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL in RFC 5847.
  • LCMPHeartbeatRetransmissionDelay: 5 seconds, and it SHOULD be less than the heartbeat interval.
  • LCMPHeartbeatMaxRetransmissions: 3. It MAY be derived from MISSING_HEARTBEATS_ALLOWED in RFC 5847.
sections.eli5: Head office keeps a settings sheet with sensible defaults, and a switch for each rule that starts in the off position. It can even keep different sheets for different groups of branches.

sections.title: How the LMA and MAG Behave
sections.content:
Both sides extend the conceptual data structures from RFC 5213, the Binding Cache Entry on the LMA and the Binding Update List entry on the MAG, to store the six LCMP values.

When the LMA receives a PBU from a MAG, it checks each enable flag. If a flag is 1 and all three matching variables are non-zero, the LMA MUST include the corresponding sub-option in the LCMP option of the PBA. If a flag is 1 but any matching variable is zero, the LMA MUST report a configuration error and reject the binding request with a PBA carrying status code 128, Reason Unspecified.

On the MAG side, a PBA that carries the Binding Re-registration Control sub-option makes the MAG MUST overwrite its locally configured re-registration timers with the received values. The Heartbeat Control sub-option works the same way for heartbeat timers. If any received parameter is zero, the MAG MUST ignore the PBA and SHOULD log an error. For the heartbeat sub-option, HB-Retransmission-Delay is the one field allowed to be zero.
sections.eli5: When a branch checks in, head office either hands back the schedule or, if its own sheet has a zero where a number belongs, says no and complains. The branch always follows the schedule it is given and ignores one that has a zero in it.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA has assigned type value 62 to the new "LMA-Controlled MAG Parameters" option in the "Mobility Options" registry, which is defined by RFC 6275. It has also created a registry named "LMA-Controlled MAG Parameters Sub-Option Type Values" and reserved the three values 0, 1 and 2. New sub-option type values are approved through Expert Review, as described in RFC 8126.
sections.eli5: A public list of numbered labels records that 62 means this option. A second list keeps track of the numbered notes that can go inside it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC notes that the LCMP option allows the configuration of re-registration and heartbeat frequencies. It is carried in Proxy Binding Update and Proxy Binding Acknowledgement messages like any other mobility header option, and the RFC concludes that it does not require any special security considerations.
sections.eli5: The note travels in the same sealed mailbag as every other message, so the RFC adds no new locks.

fields.name: LCMP Length
fields.desc: Length of the data after these two fields.

fields.name: Re-registration-Start-Time
fields.desc: Time units (4 seconds each) before binding expiry to start refreshing.

fields.name: Initial-Retransmission-Time
fields.desc: Minimum delay in seconds before the first PBU retransmission.

fields.name: Maximum-Retransmission-Time
fields.desc: Maximum delay in seconds before the last PBU retransmission.

fields.name: LCMP Length
fields.desc: Length of the data after these two fields.

fields.name: HB-Interval
fields.desc: Seconds after a successful heartbeat exchange before the next one.

fields.name: HB-Retransmission-Delay
fields.desc: Minimum seconds before a heartbeat is retransmitted.
